prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Design a high-fidelity landscape 1600 by 1000 desktop app screenshot for WARCODE, a personal AI coding agent. Edge-to-edge actual application interface, no laptop, no photograph, no browser frame, no marketing landing page.
Visual direction: an editorial production workroom translated into professional coding software. Warm ivory #F3F0E8 canvas, warm-gray #E8E3D8 sidebar, dark ink #252821, burnt orange #B94C2C primary controls, refined dark green additions in code review. Flat clean surfaces, very restrained borders, readable typography. Wordmark WARCODE in Bricolage Grotesque bold paired with an original simple W monogram. Instrument Sans body controls, IBM Plex Mono for code. Sophisticated, calm, precise, spacious where reading matters, dense where navigation matters. No paper texture, no gradients, no decorative cards, no glass, no original OpenCode O icon or word.
Structure: slim native titlebar labeled Warcode. 250px left sidebar with WARCODE at top, orange New session button, project CodingHarness, sessions Refine the workspace (selected), Fix auth callback, Add keyboard shortcuts, Settings at bottom. Broad central coding conversation, 350px right Changes panel. Header Refine the workspace with warcode-rebrand branch beneath. Conversation shows user “Simplify the project sidebar and improve keyboard navigation.” Assistant “I’ll update the sidebar structure, then check focus and keyboard navigation.” A slim Edited sidebar.tsx tool row and small genuine readable TypeScript code diff. Then “The sidebar now groups sessions by project. Keyboard focus follows the visible order.” Bottom anchored composer “Ask Warcode to build something…” with Build mode and Claude Sonnet selector and compact burnt-orange send button. Right panel has Files and Review tabs, selected sidebar.tsx and real concise TypeScript diff with green added lines and red removed lines. Thin bottom status Local workspace. All changes saved. Keep spelling sharp and exact. Use functional outline icons from one consistent set. Match a usable real coding desktop app, content is illustrative.
approval: User selected Workroom and required the existing desktop app skeleton and foundation.
